Most major European indices look set to nudge higher when trading kicks off: Euro STOXX 50 futures
are 0.3% higher and CAC futures (FCEc1) are just about in positive territory. Across the Channel though, FTSE futures (FCEc1) are a touch lower.

It looks possible, but by no means certain, that European shares will follow their counterparts in Asia and the U.S. higher. Equities have climbed ahead of U.S. jobs data later that may shed some more light on the U.S. economic backdrop. Bonds, meanwhile, have got some relief after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller dented rate-hike expectations on Thursday.
Besides the economic data, there's also some corporate news that traders will be keeping in mind.
